In 'A Sketch of the Buddha's Life: Readings from the Pali Canon', the teaching opens with this observation: *""Indeed, the Blessed One is worthy and rightly self-awakened, consummate in knowledge & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the world, unexcelled as a trainer for those people fit to be tamed, the Teacher of divine & human beings, awakened, blessed."

There is no need to search elsewhere; the truth is already here.

The text teaches: *"Perhaps I'll get an opportunity by means of the intellect.' Thus, monks, you should dwell with the doors to your senses well-guarded."
To me — resolute in exertion near the river Nerañjara, making a g"* Three levels of concentration are distinguished: (1) momentary concentration — the mind briefly settles then withdraws; (2) threshold concentration — the mind rests at its underlying level for a sustained time, often accompanied by a nimitta (sign); (3) fixed penetration (appanā samādhi) — full jhāna, where the mind abides in deep stillness endowed with applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification. Each level is a stepping stone; none should be forced. Develop mindfulness, and samādhi will arise of its own accord like water finding its level.
